text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SREs: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed across us-east-1 inference gateway — start triage. (alert id: p95-scheduler-queue-17761)
oncall-bot: metrics -> error_rate spike to 7.8% over last 3m; latency tail rising.
ian_sre: I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking scheduler queues.
maya_prod: seeing a big buildup in batching queues for model: redwood-llama-13b-quant. HEAD-OF-LINE blocking on few scheduler shards.
cheng_runtime: confirm: KV cache locks + long-lived batches. A handful of requests are holding slot and blocking batching windows.
luca_ops: any customer-visible impact metrics?
emily_support: Zendesk shows a handful of errors: multiple 502/504 gateway errors, some customers reporting timeouts on embed endpoints.
ian_sre: quick snapshot: us-east-1 gateway 5xx = 6.9% last 5m, routing retries up 3x, backlog depth on scheduler-*/batcher ~1200 per shard.
maya_prod: logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-14T15:07:02Z scheduler[pid:2345] WARN batcher: long_wait id=0x9a3 hold=4823ms requests=12 model=redwood-llama-13b-quant
2026-03-14T15:07:03Z gateway[pid:441] ERROR upstream timeout 504 conn_reset
2026-03-14T15:07:04Z scheduler[pid:2345] ERROR kvcache: lock timeout key=session:kv:7 retry=3
```
cheng_runtime: looks like two hot partitions holding KV locks -> HL-blocking. When that happens we are not completing batches and whole queue stalls.
luca_ops: can we route traffic away from those shards or enable fallback to a non-quantized variant?
ian_sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable overflow routing to fallback pool (cpu-fallback-1) 2) temporarily reduce batch window to 20ms to avoid large waiting batches 3) rate-limit heavy customers on the gateway 4) restart affected scheduler workers to break locks.
maya_prod: I'll flip overflow routing to cpu-fallback-1 for redwood-llama-13b-quant in us-east-1. Doing it now: `routes set model=redwood-llama-13b-quant region=us-east overflow=cpu-fallback-1 --reason "incident 17761"`
deploy-bot: route update applied by maya_prod at 2026-03-14T15:10:12Z (diff id: r-3342)
luca_ops: i'm increasing burst-capacity pool for dedicated customers to soak traffic while we stabilize.
cheng_runtime: reduce batch window to 20ms on affected schedulers: `sysctl redwood.batcher.window_ms=20` — will push via orchestration.
ian_sre: I'm going to identify top requesters by qps -> `top_customers=$(redis-cli zrevrange request_qps 0 10)` then throttle top 3.
emily_support: flagging top-impacted customers: acct-rodin, acct-arbor, acct-lumen — they reported >10% error rates. Outreach in progress.
maya_prod: restart of scheduler shard s-usa-7 requested to clear locks: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/scheduler-s-usa-7`. Doing controlled restart with graceful drain.
cheng_runtime: note: restarting will drop in-flight batches; overflow routing should capture most new traffic. schedule restart now.
ian_sre: running quick script to drain backlog: `./scripts/drain-batcher --shard s-usa-7 --force 60s` (monitoring).
(2m later)
maya_prod: restart finished for s-usa-7. backlog decreased from ~1200 to ~160 on that shard.
cheng_runtime: batcher window change applied across us-east schedulers. Expect fewer large batches but lower tail latency.
ian_sre: after overflow + restart + window change: gateway 5xx dropped to 2.1% in last 2m, queue depth ~420 overall.
luca_ops: continuing to add burst-capacity nodes; autoscaler still at max, applying manual scale: `scale compute-pool-burst=+8`
emily_support: customers notified: acct-rodin accepted fallback, acct-lumen requested incident timeline.
ian_sre: next step: identify root cause of KV lock hotness — see if it's an upstream NFS/metadata latency or a regression in kvcache eviction.
cheng_runtime: collecting heap/profile and KV lock traces. Attaching sampled stack in ops-trace channel.
maya_prod: can we keep overflow routing enabled for 30m then roll back if stable?
luca_ops: yes, keep for 30m and watch error rates. rolling policy to 30m.
deploy-bot: orchestration note: `routes revert` will require manual approval after 30m.
(18m later)
ian_sre: metrics check: us-east-1 gateway 5xx at 0.8% over last 5m, queue depth steady ~110, p99 latency down to baseline.
emily_support: open tickets updated; customers given ETA for postmortem.
cheng_runtime: preliminary root cause: a regression in kvcache eviction where certain session keys were not expiring due to a TTL bug after a recent deploy (release r-2026.3.11). This caused a small percentage of sessions to hold locks for minutes under certain request patterns.
maya_prod: rollback candidate: r-2026.3.11 -> r-2026.3.10 for scheduler service. Scheduling a canary rollback to one shard first.
luca_ops: agree. schedule canary rollback on s-usa-3 then monitor for lock reaccrual.
ian_sre: postmortem owners: cheng_runtime (root cause + fix), maya_prod (deployment + routing playbook), ian_sre (mitigation timeline + metrics).
emily_support: customer impact summary for internal comms: ~1.4% of total requests in us-east during spike window saw 5xx/timeouts; 25 customers had >5% error rate; top 3 customers experienced transient request failures for ~12-18 minutes.
maya_prod: making follow-up runbook additions: - auto-enable overflow if queue depth > 800 for >2m - safe restart procedure for scheduler shards - per-customer soft-throttle CLI.
cheng_runtime: patch PR created: fix TTL expiry in kvcache (PR #2786), adding unit tests and e2e for eviction edge cases.
deply-bot: PR #2786 opened by cheng_runtime -> https://git.internal/redwood/kvcache/pull/2786
(30m after initial alert)
oncall-bot: incident 1776102048 resolved -> status: mitigated, monitoring. Creator: oncall-bot.
emily_support: posting customer summary to #customer-impact and updating status page.
ian_sre: handing off to morning oncall (luca_ops) for watching; full postmortem to follow tomorrow.
luca_ops: ack, taking ownership. will watch replay for next 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
